title: Action de Galois sur Teichmüller : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting. This page belongs to Grothendieck's combinatorial description of the profinite fundamental groupoid of the projective line minus three points (P^1 − {0,1,∞}), built to describe the Galois action on the genus-0 'Teichmüller' groupoids. The base points are of two kinds:
- three points Q_i, i ∈ {0,1,∞}, attached to the three edges of the real line;
- two 'centres' P^ω, ω ∈ {+,−}, of the upper and lower hemispheres (triangles). These are the points e^{±iπ/3}, fixed by the order-3 rotation ρ.
The connecting paths are the arcs ã_i^ω and the paths d_i^ω : P^ω → Q_i. The symmetry group G_J, generated by ρ, the involutions σ_i and complex conjugation τ, permutes all of these; τ exchanges ω and ω'. The groupoid IV_J has these vertices and generators and the six relations (35). By (36)–(37) of the previous page, an automorphism u of the profinite groupoid that fixes vertices and commutes with G_J is determined by a single ξ ∈ Π̂_{0,3} (the profinite fundamental group of P^1 minus three points). The arc parameter is then α̃ = ξ·ρ^{-1}(ξ^{-1}).

This page.
1. The page opens with 'which of course implies (26)'. The NB remarks that passing from u to its conjugate τ(u) amounts to ξ ↦ σ_∞(ξ), where σ_∞ is the involution exchanging 0 and 1.
2. (38) fixes the identifications Ψ̃_i^ω : Π_{03} ≅ π_1(P^ω), with Ψ_i^ω : Π_{03} ≅ π_1(Q_i) and transport (d_i^ω)^{-1} from Q_i to P^ω.
3. (39): the relations (35) and (19) give Ψ̃_{ωi} = Ψ̃_i ∘ ρ, where ωi is the cyclic successor of i in orientation ω. Grothendieck adds a marginal query: ρ or ρ^{-1}?
4. (40): he introduces the paths d̃_i^ω = (d_i^{ω'})^{-1} d_i^ω from P^ω to P^{ω'}, i.e. go to Q_i and come back into the other hemisphere. These are permuted simply transitively by G_J.
5. (41): τ(d̃_i^ω) = d̃_i^{ω'} and d̃_i^ω d̃_i^{ω'} = 1.
6. (42): conjugation by d̃_i^ω intertwines the two identifications up to σ_∞, i.e. d̃(Ψ̃^ω(g)) = Ψ̃^{ω'}(σ_∞ g).
7. (43)–(44): the automorphism u acts by u(d̃_i^ω) = d̃_i^ω Ψ̃_i^ω(β̃), with β̃ = ξ σ_∞(ξ)^{-1}.
8. (45): therefore β̃ σ_∞(β̃) = 1. Since σ_∞ swaps the generators x and y, this is exactly the two-cycle relation f(x,y)f(y,x) = 1 of the Grothendieck–Teichmüller group GT. The relation α̃ = ξρ^{-1}(ξ)^{-1} is the analogous 'coboundary' form attached to the 3-cycle.

The next page restricts to the two vertices P^±, where the only constraint left is (47), β̃ τ_∞(β̃) = 1. It then moves on to an 11-vertex groupoid (R_i^ω, Q_i, P^ω).

Purpose. The aim is a parametrization of the Galois / GT-type automorphisms of the genus-0 building block using symmetric (non-tangential) base points at the triangle centres. In this parametrization the two-cycle and three-cycle constraints appear as 'coboundary' expressions of one parameter ξ, i.e. as nonabelian Z/2- and Z/3-cocycles.
errors: Grothendieck himself queries the convention in (39): ρ versus ρ^{-1}. This only affects the convention (ρ ↔ ρ^{-1}), not the structure.

The transcription says (41) has tildes in d̃_i^ω d̃_i^{ω'} = 1; the image seems to show d_i^ω d_i^{ω'} = 1 with the tilde notation used inconsistently. Likewise P_ξ^ω in (40) should be P^ω (the subscript is a slip or misreading).
Notation drifts between σ_∞ (this page) and τ_∞ (next page) for the same involution, and 'β̃ ci-dessus' refers to an earlier β̃ not visible here.

(45) follows from (44) only because σ_∞ is an involution and an automorphism. Conversely, every solution of (45) in the profinite free group is of the form (44) (a nonabelian H^1(Z/2, F̂_2) = 1 argument, via Z/2 ⨿ Ẑ). This converse is not stated; it would justify parametrizing by ξ.

ideas.what: Using the two symmetric points P^± (the ρ-fixed centres e^{±iπ/3} of the hemispheres) as base points of a profinite groupoid for P^1−{0,1,∞}, together with the three edge points Q_i, with the full symmetry group S_3 × complex conjugation acting.
ideas.modern_name: Fundamental groupoid with symmetric base points; the 'two-triangle' cell decomposition / dessin of P^1 minus 3 points
ideas.usually_credited_to: Grothendieck (Esquisse d'un programme, 1984) in spirit; Ihara, Nakamura, Lochak–Schneps for tangential versions
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme discusses the genus-0 'lego' and its symmetries but not these explicit formulas

ideas.what: Parametrizing a G_J-equivariant automorphism by a single ξ ∈ Π̂_{0,3}, with the cross-hemisphere parameter β̃ = ξ σ_∞(ξ)^{-1}, which automatically satisfies β̃ σ_∞(β̃) = 1.
ideas.modern_name: Two-cycle relation f(x,y)f(y,x)=1 of GT, written as a coboundary (nonabelian Z/2-cocycle)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Drinfeld 1990 (GT, including the representation f = g(y,x)^{-1}g(x,y) in the pro-unipotent setting); Ihara for the Galois version

ideas.what: α̃ = ξ ρ^{-1}(ξ)^{-1} as the analogous expression for the order-3 rotation (from the previous page).
ideas.modern_name: Three-cycle (hexagon) relation of GT in coboundary form

ideas.what: Composite paths d̃_i^ω = (d_i^{ω'})^{-1} d_i^ω between the two hemisphere centres, with the transport identity (42) twisting by σ_∞.
The NB that conjugating u by complex conjugation τ corresponds to ξ ↦ σ_∞(ξ).
ideas.modern_name: Compatibility of the Galois / GT action with complex conjugation (cf. the element (−1, 1) of GT)

missed.claim: Well before Drinfeld (1990), Grothendieck derived the two-cycle relation of GT, β̃σ_∞(β̃) = 1, in profinite form. He obtained it as a consequence of a parametrization β̃ = ξ σ_∞(ξ)^{-1} by an element ξ of the profinite fundamental group, attached to symmetric base points at the triangle centres; the analogous α̃ = ξρ^{-1}(ξ^{-1}) covers the 3-cycle.
missed.quote: (44) β̃ = ξ σ_∞(ξ)^{-1} ... satisfaisant ... la relation (45) β̃ σ_∞(β̃) = 1
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This documents that Grothendieck had, in explicit formulas, the genus-0 GT relations derived from symmetry of a base-point groupoid. A single 'potential' ξ simultaneously trivializing the Z/2 and Z/3 cocycles is reminiscent of later work on symmetric base points; it may be a slightly different parametrization of GT-type data than the standard (λ, f) one.

missed.claim: He flags, without pursuing on this page, that one should also study automorphisms permuting the vertices P^± or the Q_i, not just vertex-fixing ones. Such automorphisms would bring in the full S_3 × Z/2 equivariance and the λ-parameter.
missed.quote: il faudra regarder aussi ceux qui permutent les sommets P_∞ ou les Q_i
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This is a minor thread; vertex-permuting automorphisms correspond to known extended GT variants. Most likely nothing new.

deep.surprise_reason: The page contains an early, explicit, profinite derivation by Grothendieck of the GT two-cycle relation, in a coboundary parametrization using symmetric hemisphere-centre base points. Historically this is a notable unpublished detail predating Drinfeld. Mathematically it is now standard, and the coboundary form is known (Drinfeld, pro-unipotent case).
transcription_corrections: Line after (40): the reading 'permettant de faire simplement transition par 𝔾_m[?]' is almost certainly 'permutés de façon simplement transitive par 𝔊_J' (cf. the previous page, 'permutés transitivement par G_J').
(41): the second relation as written appears to be d_i^ω d_i^{ω'} = 1, with tildes missing in the manuscript, meaning d̃.
(39): the marginal note 'ρ^{-1}?' is Grothendieck's own query about the convention in Ψ̃^ω_i(ρg).
Marginal left: 'revenant à l'introduction de u' is attached to the NB about τ(u) ↔ σ_∞(ξ); the NB is 'NB Le passage de u à τ(u) s'exprime par ξ ↦ σ_∞(ξ) = σ̃_∞(ξ)'.
The crossed-out passage near (38) reads approximately 'Quand ... l'isom. déduit de l'isom Π_{0,3} ≅ Π_{03} pour simplifier'.
